QF.id: VIII Introduction to Clearing and Settlement System_31

question.text: In cash settlement of index derivatives, the settlement amount is:

answer.text: The difference between the contracted price and the final settlement price (for futures) or the intrinsic value based on closing index and strike (for options), settled in cash
The full notional value of the contract
The initial margin deposited by the trader
A fixed percentage of the contract value

explanation.text: The Logic: Cash-settled index futures are settled against the final settlement price - the cash flow is the difference between the previous settlement price (or trade price) and the final settlement price. Cash-settled index options are settled in cash for their intrinsic value: closing index value minus strike for calls, and strike minus closing index value for puts (subject to being in the money). No physical delivery occurs in either case. The Trap: Do not equate index option settlement with the option premium - the settlement is intrinsic value computed from the closing index price and strike, not the traded premium. Note: Source: NISM-Series-VIII workbook (Dec 2025), pages 155 and 157-158.
